The eleventh and final season of the American [[science fiction]] television series ''[[The X-Files]]'' premiered on January 3, 2018, on [[Fox Broadcasting Company|Fox]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tvline.com/news/the-x-files-season-11-premiere-date-poster-fox-886582/ |title=The X-Files Season 11 Gets January Premiere Date — See First Poster |website=[[TVLine]] |publisher=[[Penske Media Corporation|PMC]] |first=Kimberly |last=Roots |date=November 15, 2017 |access-date=November 15, 2017}}</ref> The season consists of ten episodes and concluded on March 21, 2018. It follows newly re-instated [[Federal Bureau of Investigation]] (FBI) agents [[Fox Mulder]] ([[David Duchovny]]) and [[Dana Scully]] ([[Gillian Anderson]]). The season's storyline picks up directly after last season's [[My Struggle II|finale]] and the search for Mulder and Scully's son [[Baby William|William]] is the main story arc of the season.<ref name="ign"/>

==Plot overview==
[[Dana Scully]] ([[Gillian Anderson]]) wakes up in the hospital after having a seizure, now realizing the events of "[[My Struggle II]]" were a vision and haven't actually happened yet. Mulder initially presumes Scully’s ramblings are a product of her illness but leaves the hospital to investigate. Agent [[Jeffrey Spender]] later appears at Scully’s bedside, revealing that someone is looking for [[Baby William|William]]. He first balks at telling her the location of her son, revealing only the name of the family that adopted him—[[William (The X-Files)|Van De Kamp]]. Mulder tails a henchman who he believes will take him to The Smoking Man, but he arrives somewhere else with mysterious conspirators; Mr. Y (A.C. Peterson) and Erika Price ([[Barbara Hershey]]). 

They try to negotiate with Mulder into turning over his son but Mulder refuses. [[Walter Skinner]] ([[Mitch Pileggi]]) tries to meet with Scully, but can't find her. As he goes to his car, he is met inside by The Smoking Man and Reyes. Meanwhile, Scully tries to leave the hospital but her seizures return causing her to crash her car. She is rescued by Agent Einstein and Agent Miller, and is readmitted to the hospital. Both agents leave the room. An assassin sent by Mr. Y and Erika enters and tries to suffocate Scully, but Mulder steps in and saves her by slicing the assassin's neck. As Skinner comes in, Mulder confronts him since he smells like smoke. In a flashback to when Skinner was in the car with the Smoking Man, the latter reveals, in a further flashback to 17 years, "[[En Ami]]", that ''he'', not Mulder, artificially impregnated Scully.<ref>{{cite episode |title=My Struggle III |series=The X-Files |series-link=The X-Files |credits=[[Chris Carter (screenwriter)|Chris Carter]] (director); [[Chris Carter (screenwriter)|Chris Carter]] (writer) |network=[[Fox Broadcasting Company|Fox]] |season=11 |number=1}}</ref>

Scully opens her eyes in the dark, lying on her side on a bed in a mysterious house. She explores the mysterious house and ends up in an endless pattern of the same room. Mulder theorizes that the experience is a type of sleep paralysis. She goes back to her memories of her sleep paralysis, where she grabs a snow globe with a model of the boat in it. Mulder and Scully get to the dock, meeting with Detective Costa ([[Louis Ferreira]]). Later, Scully’s attention is drawn to a man that observes them intently from one of the portable walkways. Costa informs them that the victims asked if they found Ghouli. When Scully turns to check if the mystery guy is there, he’s gone. 

Both agents investigate the two teenagers about the slashing. Both of them go on about the experience and their boyfriend, Jackson Van De Kamp. The agents arrive at the Van De Kamp household, the same house Scully saw in her dream. Two gunshots are heard with a third coming from upstairs. Scully goes up and finds the bleeding corpse of Jackson Van De Kamp. As they leave the room and the door clicks closed, the zipper opens slowly. Jackson sits up and escapes the room. Mulder meets with Skinner at the Chimera, telling him to drop the investigation. Mulder confirms that Jackson's DNA matches Scully's. 

At the hospital, Jackson explains to Brianna that he’s been hiding because there are people after him. He reveals that Ghouli doesn't exist and it's just something he "made up". Jackson escapes the hospital after the death of the DOD members. The next day, Scully spots a rural gas station that has a windmill just outside. Scully meets with Peter Wong with Wong mentioning that he wishes he could know her better. The agents ask to see the recording tapes. In the recording, Scully is having a conversation with William. She smiles as Mulder holds her while they see their son, alive.<ref>{{cite episode |title=Ghouli |series=The X-Files |series-link=The X-Files |credits=[[James Wong (filmmaker)|James Wong]] (director); [[James Wong (filmmaker)|James Wong]] (writer) |network=[[Fox Broadcasting Company|Fox]] |season=11 |number=5}}</ref> Over the course of the season, they search for William. In the third episode of the "[[Plus One (The X-Files)|Plus One]]", Scully and Mulder are intimate again. In the season 11 finale, "[[My Struggle IV]]", she reveals to Mulder that she is pregnant with his child. Also in the finale, the Smoking Man shoots William, who has made himself look like Mulder.

==Cast==
===Main cast===
*[[David Duchovny]] as [[Fox Mulder]], an FBI special agent assigned to the newly reopened X-Files division. He remains a believer in the paranormal and the existence of extraterrestrial life, though, throughout the series, his faith begins to waver. 
*[[Gillian Anderson]] as [[Dana Scully]], a medical doctor and FBI special agent assigned to the X-Files. Although an initial skeptic, after Mulder's abduction, she became more open-minded about the possibility of extraterrestrial life. 
*[[Mitch Pileggi]] as [[Walter Skinner]], an assistant director at the FBI and an ally of Mulder and Scully's.{{efn|Only credited for the episodes he appears in.}}

{{notelist}}

===Recurring cast===
*[[William B. Davis]] as [[Cigarette Smoking Man]], a former government official, and nemesis of Mulder and Scully, who worked to cover up the truth of the existence of aliens and their plan to colonize the Earth. Jeremy Schuetze portrays a younger version of this character in flashbacks.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tvline.com/news/the-x-files-trailer-season-11-second-revival-video-874369/ |title=X-Files Trailer Confirms Second Revival Is All About [Spoiler] — Watch Now |website=TVLine |first=Michael |last=Ausiello |date=October 8, 2017 |access-date=October 10, 2017}}</ref>
*[[Barbara Hershey]] as Erika Price<ref>{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2017/08/the-x-files-barbara-hershey-cast-season-11-fox-series-1202148572/ |title='The X-Files': Barbara Hershey Joins Season 11 Of Fox Series |website=Deadline Hollywood |first=Nellie |last=Andreeva |date=August 14, 2017 |access-date=August 15, 2017}}</ref>
*[[Miles Robbins]] as [[Baby William|Jackson Van De Kamp/William Scully]], the son of Dana Scully who was placed for adoption.

===Guest cast===
*[[Annabeth Gish]] as [[Monica Reyes]], a former FBI agent previously assigned to the X-Files division.
*[[James Pickens Jr.]] as [[Alvin Kersh]], the [[Deputy Director of the FBI]]
*[[Lauren Ambrose]] as Agent Liz Einstein, a medical doctor, Miller's partner, and a hard-skeptic.
*[[Robbie Amell]] as Agent Kyd Miller, an open-minded FBI agent who believes in the paranormal, and is Einstein's partner.
*[[Chris Owens (actor)|Chris Owens]] as [[Jeffrey Spender]]<ref name="fansided">{{cite web |url=https://fansided.com/2017/10/08/nycc-2017-watch-x-files-season-11-trailer-now/ |title=NYCC 2017: Watch The X-Files season 11 trailer now |website=Fansided |last=Frederick |first=Brittany |date=October 8, 2017 |access-date=October 9, 2017 |archive-date=October 10, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171010005249/https://fansided.com/2017/10/08/nycc-2017-watch-x-files-season-11-trailer-now/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>
*[[Dean Haglund]] as Langly, one of [[The Lone Gunmen]].<ref name="fansided"/>
*[[Haley Joel Osment]] as Davey James<ref>{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2017/10/the-x-files-haley-joel-osment-guest-star-fox-event-series-1202198304/ |title='The X-Files': Haley Joel Osment To Guest Star In Fox Event Series |website=Deadline Hollywood |first=Denise |last=Petski |date=October 31, 2017 |access-date=October 31, 2017}}</ref>
*[[Joel McHale]] as Tad O'Malley

==Production==
In May 2015, in an interview with ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]'', co-star [[David Duchovny]] stated that if the [[The X-Files season 10|2016 revival]] were successful, he would be interested in another renewal, stating, "I would be open to doing another cycle. I don't know that I could do a 20-episode version of this show at this point in my life, and I don't know that Gillian could. But I think everybody is open ended on what happens after this. Certainly, we didn't bring it back with the idea of ending it."<ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Hibberd |first1=James |title=''The X-Files'': David Duchovny Says the New Script Made Him Cry |url=https://www.ew.com/article/2015/05/26/x-files-david-duchovny |magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]] |access-date=October 1, 2015 |date=May 26, 2015}}</ref> At the 2016 [[Television Critics Association]] panel for the series, creator [[Chris Carter (screenwriter)|Chris Carter]] stated, "If we do well in the ratings, I can't imagine we wouldn't be asked to do more."<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.ew.com/article/2016/01/15/x-files-tca |title=''X-Files'' Creator Admits Second Movie Was a Misstep |magazine=Entertainment Weekly |date=January 15, 2016 |access-date=January 17, 2016 |last=Hibberd |first=James}}</ref> 

Fox Television Group chairman and CEO Gary Newman stated that he and fellow executive Dana Walden would be open to another renewal, stating, "We would love to do this again, so we'd be on board if schedules can be worked out."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://variety.com/2016/tv/news/the-x-files-revival-new-season-future-show-renew-chances-1201680907/ |title='The X-Files' Creator Says Revival Is a Chance to 'Prove That the Show Has More Life' In It |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |first=Laura |last=Prudom |date=January 15, 2016 |access-date=January 27, 2016}}</ref> In an interview with ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'' prior to the premiere, co-star [[Gillian Anderson]], Duchovny, and Walden stated their willingness for another renewal.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://variety.com/2016/tv/features/x-files-revival-fox-david-duchovny-gillian-anderson-1201682379/ |title='The X-Files': How Fox Revived Mulder and Scully's Search for the Truth |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |first=Geoff |last=Berkshire |date=January 19, 2016 |access-date=February 4, 2016}}</ref> In an interview with ''[[TV Guide]]'', Carter reaffirmed plans for more episodes, but stressed that everyone involved is waiting on the success of the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tvguide.com/news/the-x-files-revival-chris-carter/ |title=The X-Files' Chris Carter Is Already Preparing for More Episodes |work=[[TV Guide]] |first=Sadie |last=Gennis |date=January 21, 2016 |access-date=February 4, 2016}}</ref> In May 2016, Walden confirmed that there had been conversations about an eleventh season possibly for the 2017–18 television season.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Ausiello |first1=Michael |title=The X-Files Update: David Duchovny, Gillian Anderson, Chris Carter 'On Board' For Season 11, Per Fox CEO |url=http://tvline.com/2016/05/16/the-x-files-season-11-fox-premiere-date-more-episodes/ |website=[[TVLine]] |access-date=May 20, 2016 |date=May 16, 2016 |archive-date=May 20, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160520223152/http://tvline.com/2016/05/16/the-x-files-season-11-fox-premiere-date-more-episodes/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On April 20, 2017, Fox announced that ''The X-Files'' would be returning for an eleventh season of ten episodes, which would air in the [[2017–18 United States network television schedule|2017–18 television season]] after filming in mid-2017.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2017/04/x-files-returns-event-series-fox-1202073290/ |title='The X-Files' Coming Back Again For New Event Series Next Season |website=Deadline Hollywood |first=Dominic |last=Patten |date=April 20, 2017 |access-date=April 21, 2017}}</ref>

===Writing===
The writing staff for the eleventh season consists of Chris Carter, [[Glen Morgan]], [[Darin Morgan]], [[James Wong (filmmaker)|James Wong]], and newcomers who were all previously part of ''The X-Files'' production staff, [[Gabe Rotter]] (writers assistant), Benjamin Van Allen (writers assistant) and Brad Follmer (Carter's personal assistant).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tvline.com/news/the-x-files-season-11-writers-darin-morgan-james-wong-842995/ |title=The X-Files Season 11 Writers Revealed: Who's Back? Who's Missing? |website=[[TVLine]] |publisher=[[Penske Media Corporation|PMC]] |first=Michael |last=Ausiello |date=June 26, 2017 |access-date=June 26, 2017}}</ref> In August 2017, it was announced that three female writers were added to the staff. Karen Nielsen, who worked as a script coordinator on season 10, wrote one episode, and [[Kristen Cloke]] and Shannon Hamblin wrote another episode based on a story by Glen Morgan.<ref name="s11update">{{cite web |url=http://tvline.com/2017/08/07/the-x-files-season-11-women-directors-female/ |title=The X-Files Season 11 Update: 2 Female Directors Join Fox Revival |website=TVLine |first=Michael |last=Ausiello |date=August 7, 2017 |access-date=August 8, 2017 |archive-date=August 8, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170808061843/http://tvline.com/2017/08/07/the-x-files-season-11-women-directors-female/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.indiewire.com/2017/08/the-x-files-season-11-women-writers-mythology-episodes-william-1201864653/ |title='The X-Files' Season 11 Adds Women Writers and Directors, Plus More Details on Show's Return [UPDATED] |website=IndieWire |first=Liz Shannon |last=Miller |date=August 8, 2017 |access-date=January 27, 2018}}</ref> The season, consisting of 10 episodes, has two [[Mythology of The X-Files|mythology episodes]] (the premiere and finale) and eight standalone episodes;<ref name="ign">{{cite web |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2017/08/08/what-to-expect-from-the-x-files-season-11 |title=What to Expect from The X-Files: Season 11 |website=[[IGN]] |publisher=[[Ziff Davis, LLC]] |first=Terri |last=Schwartz |date=August 8, 2017 |access-date=August 9, 2017}}</ref> however, several critics have considered episode five, "[[Ghouli]]", to also be a mythology episode.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.denofgeek.com/tv/the-x-files-season-11-episode-5-review-ghouli/ |title=The X-Files Season 11 Episode 5 Review: Ghouli |website=Den of Geek |first=Chris |last=Longo |date=January 31, 2018 |access-date=March 8, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.indiewire.com/2018/01/x-files-review-season-11-episode-5-ghouli-spoilers-william-1201923881/ |title='The X-Files' Review: Confusing But Compelling 'Ghouli' Looks Like a Casefile, But Ends Up Being More |website=IndieWire |first=Liz Shannon |last=Miller |date=January 31, 2018 |access-date=March 8, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.avclub.com/scully-has-strange-dreams-on-a-twisty-x-files-1822598635 |title=Scully has strange dreams on a twisty X-Files |website=The A.V. Club |first=Zack |last=Handlen |date=January 31, 2018 |access-date=March 8, 2018}}</ref>

===Casting===
In addition to Duchovny and Anderson, [[Mitch Pileggi]] was confirmed to reprise his role, as [[Walter Skinner]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2017/07/the-x-files-mitch-pileggi-return-season-11-fox-1202131665/ |title='The X-Files': Mitch Pileggi Set To Return For Season 11 Of Fox Series |website=Deadline Hollywood |first=Nellie |last=Andreeva |date=July 19, 2017 |access-date=August 8, 2017}}</ref> Also returning are [[William B. Davis]] as [[Cigarette Smoking Man]] and [[Annabeth Gish]] as [[Monica Reyes]].<ref name="ign"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://screenrant.com/x-files-annabeth-gish-announces-season-11-return/ |title=X-Files: Annabeth Gish Announces Season 11 Return |website=Screen Rant |first=Michael |last=Kennedy |date=August 7, 2017 |access-date=August 9, 2017}}</ref> In August 2017, it was confirmed that [[Robbie Amell]] and [[Lauren Ambrose]] would reprise their roles Agents Miller and Einstein from season ten.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tvline.com/casting-news/the-x-files-season-11-robbie-amell-lauren-ambrose-returning-857549/ |title=The X-Files Season 11: Robbie Amell and Lauren Ambrose Returning |website=TVLine |first=Michael |last=Ausiello |date=August 14, 2017 |access-date=August 14, 2017}}</ref> In September 2017, it was announced that [[Karin Konoval]]–who played Mrs. Peacock in the fourth-season episode "[[Home (The X-Files)|Home]]"–would play new characters in the eleventh season, in what Carter described as a "tour-de-force performance".<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://ew.com/tv/2017/09/22/x-files-karin-konoval-home/ |title=X-Files actress who played show's most notorious role to return |magazine=Entertainment Weekly |first=James |last=Hibberd |date=September 22, 2017 |access-date=September 22, 2017}}</ref> 

Anderson commented that this is her final season of ''The X-Files'', saying, "I've said from the beginning this is it for me."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tvinsider.com/654662/the-x-files-season-11-exclusive-interview-gillian-anderson-david-duchovny/ |title=Inside 'The X-Files' Season 11: Mulder and Scully Take on Their Biggest Mystery Yet |last=Roffman |first=Marisa |date=December 20, 2017 |website=TV Insider |access-date=January 1, 2018}}</ref> However, Chris Carter affirmed he would not do ''The X-Files'' without her character, saying, "For me, ''The X-Files'' is Mulder and Scully. I think if it were without Scully, I wouldn't do it. That's not my ''X-Files''."<ref>{{cite web |url=http://tvline.com/2018/01/03/the-x-files-season-12-gillian-anderson-leaving-scully/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180104053236/http://tvline.com/2018/01/03/the-x-files-season-12-gillian-anderson-leaving-scully/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 4, 2018 |title=Chris Carter on Gillian Anderson Exit Buzz: There Is No X-Files Without Scully |website=TVLine |first=Michael |last=Ausiello |date=January 3, 2018 |access-date=January 4, 2018}}</ref> The writers intended to bring back [[Robert Patrick]] as his character [[John Doggett]], but he was unavailable due to scheduling issues as he was filming for his TV series ''[[Scorpion (TV series)|Scorpion]]''.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.goldderby.com/article/2018/the-x-files-robert-patrick-john-doggett-season-11-news/ |title='The X-Files' wanted Robert Patrick back as John Doggett for Season 11, but 'scheduling issue' got in the way |website=GoldDerby |first=Marcus James |last=Dixon |date=January 10, 2018 |access-date=January 27, 2018}}</ref>  In February 2018, Carter stated in an interview that he could see the show continuing without Anderson.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.digitalspy.com/tv/the-x-files/interviews/a849103/x-files-chris-carter-season-11-gillian-anderson/ |title=X-Files' Chris Carter interview: 'The X-Files has more life in it – with or without Gillian Anderson' |first=Mayer |last=Nissim |website=Digital Spy.com |date=February 5, 2018 |access-date=February 7, 2018}}</ref>

===Filming===
Filming began in August 2017 in [[Vancouver]], British Columbia, where the previous season was filmed, along with the show's original five seasons.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://vancouversun.com/news/local-news/david-duchovny-x-files-return-to-vancouver-as-shooting-for-11th-season-begins |title=David Duchovny, X-Files return to Vancouver as shooting for 11th season begins |work=Vancouver Sun |first=Harrison |last=Mooney |date=August 3, 2017 |access-date=August 8, 2017}}</ref> After controversy sparked regarding the lack of female writers or directors on the series, it was announced in August 2017 that Carol Banker, a script supervisor on the original series who also directed an episode of ''[[The Lone Gunmen (TV series)|The Lone Gunmen]]'' and [[Holly Dale]] were added as directors.<ref name="s11update"/>

==Reception==
===Critical reviews===
The eleventh season received generally positive reviews from critics and currently has a [[Metacritic]] score of 67 out of 100 based on 18 reviews.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.metacritic.com/tv/the-x-files/season-11 |title=The X-Files - Season 11 Reviews |website=Metacritic |publisher=[[CBS Interactive|CBS Interactive Inc.]] |access-date=January 4, 2017}}</ref> On [[Rotten Tomatoes]], the season has an approval rating of 77% with an average rating of 6.65 out of 10 based on 170 reviews. The site's consensus reads, "Though it may not make many new believers, ''The X-Files'' return to business as usual is a refreshing upgrade from the show's underwhelming previous outing."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/tv/the_x_files/s11 |title=The X-Files: Season 11 |website=Rotten Tomatoes |access-date=January 16, 2017}}</ref> Similar to season 10, the premiere and finale episodes of season 11 received poor reviews, while the stand-alone episodes occurring between them were much more favorably received.<ref name=rotten_tomatoes/>

Based on the first five episodes available for review, Liz Shannon Miller of ''[[IndieWire]]'' gave the season a positive review with a "B+" grade. While Miller wrote that the season premiere "is not good", she was much more positive of the following four standalone episodes, writing that "there are some intriguing mysteries, some eerie moments, solid action" and praised Darin Morgan's comedy installment, calling it "fantastic". Overall, she concluded, "Season 11 so far isn't flawless, but it's a lively, character-focused affair that feels far more unified than we'd ever anticipated, a massive improvement over Season 10 that gives us genuine hope for the second half. For the first time in a while, we're truly excited to see more."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.indiewire.com/2017/12/x-files-season-11-review-1201908214/ |title='The X-Files' Season 11 Review: Mulder and Scully Return, and The Results Are Genuinely Exciting |website=IndieWire |first=Liz Shannon |last=Miller |date=December 15, 2017 |access-date=December 15, 2017}}</ref> 

[[Matt Zoller Seitz]] of ''[[New York (magazine)#Digital|Vulture]]'' stated that compared to the [[The X-Files season 10|previous season]], "This new batch of episodes is considerably stronger. Even the ones that don't really do much but spin their wheels do so with feeling, and when the show is great—as it is, yet again, in Darin Morgan's episode—it's downright sublime."<ref>{{cite web |last1=Seitz |first1=Matt Zoller |author-link1=Matt Zoller Seitz |title=The X-Files Is Sublime in Season 11 |url=https://www.vulture.com/2018/01/the-x-files-season-11-review.html |website=[[New York (magazine)#Digital|Vulture]] |publisher=[[New York (magazine)|New York Media LLC]] |access-date=January 4, 2018 |date=January 3, 2018}}</ref>
